title: r1 W1 fix landed only halfway: the two em-dash strings were rewritten, but the claimed no_em_dash_test extension to scan refcheck copy never happened
evidence: no_em_dash_test still iterates for_each_copy = all_codes() x all_contexts() (toast/page copy only). grep across client/test finds no refcheck-const scan and no em-dash assertion over copy.gleam's refcheck section; client/test/copy_test.gleam never references refcheck consts. The two r1-flagged strings ARE rewritten dash-free (refcheck_unmoderated_flag = 'Unmoderated referee text: written by the referee, not reviewed by us.'; refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed = 'Applicant nudge: couldn't send'), so the shipped defect is gone — but the durable pin the r1 fix map claims ('no_em_dash_test extended to scan refcheck consts') is absent: any implementer-authored em-dash reintroduced into the panel copy (timeline labels, new states, future consts) sails through CI.
detail: r1 W1 recommended_fix had two halves: rewrite the strings AND extend the ban test. Only the first half landed. Note the extension is non-trivial: 10+ refcheck consts deliberately carry spec-verbatim em-dashes (§7.4/§7.5/§10.3/§7.8 — verified byte-for-byte in ux-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md), so a naive blanket scan would fail; the fix needs a spec-verbatim allowlist or a scan of implementer-authored strings only (timeline/pill/slot/off/explainer-title consts + the batch_line ' — ' channel join).
recommended_fix: Extend the em-dash pin to the refcheck copy with a spec-verbatim allowlist (or scan only implementer-authored consts), e.g. iterate the refcheck_* consts and panic on any dash not in the allowlisted §7.4/§7.5/§10.3/§7.8 strings.

title: r1 N10 signal-sentence tests landed 6 of 7: the geo-mismatch sentence is still unpinned — no fixture drives geo_vs_claimed_property 'inconsistent'
evidence: worth_knowing_signals has an arm for geo_vs_claimed_property == 'inconsistent' -> copy.refcheck_signal_geo_mismatch ('Filled in from a location that doesn't match the property's area...'). All three signal fixtures in the panel tests use "geo_vs_claimed_property":"unknown" (lines 111, 634, 972); grep for 'doesn't match the property' / 'inconsistent' in client/test finds no assertion. The remaining 6 sentences are pinned (fast_completion in worth_knowing_renders_with_signal_test; same_device/voip/duplicate/within/across in remaining_signal_sentences_render_test).
detail: The r1 note asked for per-signal sentence tests; the rework added them but omitted the geo branch — exactly the class of mapping branch where a copy typo hides silently.
recommended_fix: Add a fixture with "geo_vs_claimed_property":"inconsistent" and assert the refcheck_signal_geo_mismatch sentence renders.

title: nudge_label's skipped/failed arms are untested — the W1-rewritten timeline labels have no pin at all
evidence: nudge_label branches: all-delivered -> refcheck_timeline_nudge ('Applicant asked to nudge'), skipped-found -> refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> ' — ' <> detail, else refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed ('Applicant nudge: couldn't send'). The only nudge assertion in the panel tests is 'Applicant asked to nudge' (delivered arm, line 359). grep confirms 'nudge skipped' and "couldn't send" appear nowhere in client/test.
detail: The two labels r1 W1 forced to be rewritten ('Applicant nudge: couldn't send', 'Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}') are exactly the ones whose final wording is unpinned — a regression back to an em-dash or rewording would not fail any test.
recommended_fix: Add a co-nudge batch fixture with outcome 'skipped' (assert 'Applicant nudge skipped' + the detail join) and one with outcome 'failed' (assert 'Applicant nudge: couldn't send').

title: r1 N2 fix (normalize_datetime) landed in code but has zero test coverage — the PG ' ' -> 'T' conversion path never executes in any test
evidence: normalize_datetime (string.replace(at, ' ', 'T')) is only exercised when the at-value is Postgres ::text form ('2026-08-01 21:12:00+00'). Every test fixture timestamp is RFC3339 'T'-form (invite_attempt at '2026-08-01T10:04:00Z', form_opened_at '2026-08-01T21:12:00Z', the integration pin rides the raw PG form only on the server wire), so the replacement is a no-op in all tests. No test asserts a datetime= attribute at all (grep 'datetime' in reference_panel_test.gleam: no matches).
detail: The r1 N2 defect (invalid HTML datetime for the Form-opened line) is fixed in code, but the exact conversion that fixes it is unpinned: a regression dropping the normalization would ship invalid datetime attributes and no test would notice.
recommended_fix: Add a Form-opened fixture with a space-form timestamp ('2026-08-01 21:12:00+00') and assert the serialized <time datetime="2026-08-01T21:12:00+00"> attribute.

title: First-view auto-expand handler test covers only the FormCompleted branch — ManualRecorded and Partial arms of the summary filter are untested
evidence: The filter expands FormCompleted | ManualRecorded | Partial. refcheck_first_view_auto_expands_completed_rows_test builds one FormCompleted row (rc-1, expands) and one Queued row (rc-2, does not). No update-level test constructs ManualRecorded or Partial rows; a regression dropping either arm from the filter would pass all tests.
detail: The r1 W8 fix (auto-expand gating + toggle + route reset) is genuinely landed and well tested, but the per-status filter arms are only partially covered. Panel-level render tests do cover ManualRecorded/Partial rows expanding when already in the set, so this is a narrow P3 boundary gap.
recommended_fix: Extend refcheck_first_view_auto_expands_completed_rows_test with ManualRecorded and Partial rows asserting they join refcheck_expanded on first view.

title: Notable-quotes truncation boundary untested: list.take(3) cap is never exercised with more than 3 quotes
evidence: notable_quotes_render_when_present_test uses exactly 3 quotes and asserts all three render. No fixture carries 4+ quotes, so the take(3) truncation (the AC3 '≤3 notable quotes' cap) is unpinned — a regression removing the cap (or capping at 2) would not fail.
detail: Small P3 boundary gap in the fresh trace of the completed-summary surface; the presence path is tested, the cap is not.
recommended_fix: Add a 4-quote fixture asserting the fourth is absent from the serialized render.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
evidence: Fix audit: B1 hook-driven terminality (all_terminal_subline_test), W2 word map ('landlord' pin + choice_word_map_is_total_test — the 29-value list verified complete against server/src/reference_checks/questions.gleam's Choice/ChoiceWithOther tuples), W3 relationship_other, W4 chronological timeline, W5 gender-neutral objected, W6 localStorage dismissal, W7 6-of-6 character count, W8 handler tests (toggle/auto-expand/not-consumed-gate/route-reset), N9 5-token never-red, N10 object branches, N11 integration wire pins (null + stamped), N12 v2/malformed/aria tests — all verified present and meaningful by reading this worktree (e0f9fa7). Suites verified green in this worktree: make test-client 521 passed, make test-shared 108 passed. P0 gaps: none (12-state matrix, testids, back-compat decoder, strip guards, auto-expand gating all covered). P1 gaps: one — the em-dash pin still does not scan refcheck copy (r1 W1 test-extension half missing). P3: geo signal sentence, nudge-label error arms, normalize_datetime, auto-expand ManualRecorded/Partial arms, quote-truncation cap.
detail: P0 100%; P1 sits in the 80-89% band only because of the single unresolved em-dash-pin gap from r1; overall behaviour coverage is well above 90% (44 panel render tests + 6 update-level handler tests + shared round-trip/back-compat + server encoder + integration wire pins). The r1 warning-level coverage findings (W8) are genuinely closed; the remaining named gap is the W1 test extension.
recommended_fix: Close the W1 test-extension gap (scan implementer-authored refcheck consts with a spec-verbatim allowlist) to reach PASS; the P3 notes (geo signal, nudge error labels, datetime normalization, auto-expand filter arms, quote cap) are cheap follow-ups that would harden the panel further.
